notes.meaning: Long ago, false prophets showed up among the people of Israel, and in the same way false teachers will arise in the church. They will secretly bring in harmful lies and turn against the Lord, bringing quick ruin upon their own heads. Believers must stay alert so they are not led astray by distorted messages.

differ.view: Christ gave His life for everyone, so even those who deny Him were truly bought by His sacrifice before they turned away to ruin.
The false teachers were bought only by their own outward claim to follow Christ, not because they were truly chosen or redeemed by His blood.

notes.meaning: Many people will follow these corrupt leaders into immoral living. Because people see such bad behavior among professed believers, outsiders will insult the Christian faith and speak evil of God's truth.

These deceitful teachers care mainly about money and will take advantage of others using made-up stories. God made up His mind to judge such wicked leaders long ago, and their punishment will not sleep.
God did not let even angels escape punishment when they rebelled against Him. Instead, He threw them down into gloomy, dark pits to hold them safely until the final judgment day.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Ancient Jewish tradition connected these fallen angels to the heavenly beings who sinned with human women in Genesis before the great flood.

notes.meaning: God also wiped out the ancient world when He brought the great flood over ungodly humanity. Even so, He protected Noah, who preached what was right, and spared seven other members of Noah's family.

God reduced the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to piles of ashes because of their deep wickedness. This complete destruction was placed in history as a clear warning of what will happen to anyone who rejects God.

God showed mercy by rescuing Lot, a man who remained faithful to Him despite the terrible sin all around him. Living in Sodom caused Lot constant mental anguish every day because of the lawless things he was forced to see and hear.

These past events prove that the Lord always knows the right way to save His faithful people from their troubles. At the same time, He knows how to keep unrighteous people under custody until their final punishment.

God's heaviest judgment will fall on people who follow dirty physical cravings and treat all authority with contempt. They are reckless and proud, showing no fear even when they insult powerful spiritual beings.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars suggest the "glorious beings" here are angels rather than human rulers.

notes.meaning: Even the holy angels, who have far more strength and authority than any human, do not act with such disrespect. When they stand before the Lord, they refuse to speak insulting accusations against spiritual beings.

These corrupt teachers act like wild animals that have no common sense and live only by raw instinct. They boldly curse things they do not understand, and like wild beasts, they will be caught and destroyed in their own filth.

They will reap the exact harm they caused to others as their proper reward. Without any shame, they party wildly in broad daylight and bring disgrace to the church while sharing fellowship meals with true believers.

Their eyes constantly search for someone to commit sexual sin with, and their craving for evil never stops. They bait and trap Christians who are not grounded in the truth, because their hearts are completely trained in greed.
They have abandoned the straight, honest path and gone totally off course. They are following the bad example of Balaam, who cared more about making money from wickedness than obeying God.
Balaam was firmly stopped in his sinful direction by his own riding donkey. God miraculously caused the mute beast to speak with a human voice to halt the prophet's greedy madness.

These false leaders are like dried-up water springs that offer nothing to a thirsty traveler. They are like clouds pushed along by a fierce storm that drop no useful rain, and total darkness is waiting for them in eternity.

They use boastful, fancy words that sound impressive but have no real truth in them. By offering excuses for bodily desires, they trap brand new converts who have barely broken free from their old pagan habits.

These teachers tell people they can do whatever they want and call it freedom. In reality, they are trapped slaves to their own dirty habits, because a person is always a slave to whatever controls them.

People may learn about Jesus Christ and leave the evil ways of the world behind for a while. But if they get pulled back in and conquered by those old sins, their final situation is much worse than when they started.

differ.view: True believers who have genuinely escaped sin through real faith in Christ can turn back, become enslaved again, and lose their salvation.
The people described only changed their outer habits through learning about Jesus, but they never possessed true saving faith or a transformed heart.

notes.meaning: It would have been much better for them never to have learned God's true way in the first place. Knowing the holy commandments and then turning their backs on them brings far greater guilt and heavier judgment.

Their return to sin proves that their inner nature was never truly made new. They fit the well-known proverbs about a dog going back to eat its own vomit and a clean pig running straight back to roll in the mud.

differ.view: The dog stayed a dog and the pig stayed a pig. These people never had a real change of heart. True believers still sin, but they do not fall away from God's grace.
These people had truly repented and been washed, which shows that a real believer can fall from grace.
